answer: Each identity must custody one unique shard of the river dataset and stake 40 credits. A kernel assigns the shard and auditors issue retrieval challenges; a hollow shard, an empty or copied file, fails the hash check, slashing its stake. A rented farm fails when simultaneous challenges to identities sharing one node time out or return identical hashes. The k-th fake still pays 40 staked plus a 10 credit audit fee, so 1,000 fakes cost 50,000 credits with no reuse discount. An honest agent keeps one shard, pays 10 credits once, and recovers its stake after a clean epoch.
